catalog_quote: इतर भाषेप्रमाणे वऱ्हाडीतही असे काही स्वनिम आहेत की, जे स्वतंत्रपणे उच्चारता येत नाहीत. त्यांचा उच्चार खंडित स्वनिमांबरोबरच करावा लागतो. अशा स्वनिमांना पराखंडकीय स्वनिम म्हणतात. बल, सीमक, सुरयोजन आणि नासिक्यरंजन हे पराखंडीय स्वनिम आहेत. यादृष्टीने वऱ्हाडीचे विवेचन पुढीलप्रमाणे- (अ) बल : १. प्रबल बल : वऱ्हाडी बोलीत प्रबल बलाचा वापर होतो. उदा० १) बंडि वावरात नेलि / ( बैलगाडी शेतात नेली.) - "बैलगाडी कुठे गेली?" या श्रोत्याच्या प्रश्नाला उत्तर देताना वक्ता 'वावरात' या शब्दावर प्रबल बल देतो. २) बंडि वावरात नेलि / ( बैलगाडी शेतात नेली.) - "शेतात काय नेल?" या श्रोत्याच्या प्रश्नाला उत्तर देताना वक्ता 'बंडि' या शब्दावर बल देत असतो. ३) फुइले इव्यान मारल / ( आत्याला विड्याने मारले.) - "कशाने मारले?" इव्यान् मार्ले / "कोणाला मारले?" - फुइले. २. अतिप्रबल बल : उदा० १) आप्ल्या धुऱ्यावरचि काटि तोळ्ळि / ( आपल्या बांधावरची बाभुळी तोडली.) दुसऱ्याच्या तोडली नाही, याअर्थाने ( ल् - य् - आ) मधील 'आ' वर अतिप्रबल बल दिला जातो. ... ३. तुटक बल : उदा० १) काल् रात्रि आल्तो / ( काल रात्री आलो होतो.) हे वाक्य तुटक बलाने काल् रात्ति आल्तो / ( काल रात्रीच आलो होतो.) ... ४. विलंबित बल : उदा० १) गाव्हि व : / ( गायकी गाईला हाक मारना.)

new_statements.translation: Stress (bal), juncture (simak), intonation (surayojan) and nasalization are the suprasegmental phonemes. Varhadi is treated from this angle as follows. (a) Stress: 1. Strong stress: strong stress is used in the Varhadi dialect. E.g. 1) baṇḍi vāvrāt neli / ('the bullock-cart was taken to the field') — when answering the listener's question 'Where did the bullock-cart go?', the speaker puts strong stress on the word 'vāvrāt'. 2) baṇḍi vāvrāt neli — when answering the question 'What was taken to the field?', the speaker puts stress on the word 'baṇḍi'. [...] 2. Extra-strong stress: e.g. 1) āplyā dhunyāvarci kāṭi toḷḷi / ('the babhul tree on our own bund was cut') — in the sense 'not somebody else's', extra-strong stress is put on the 'ā' of (l-y-ā) [i.e. on the last syllable of āplyā 'own'].

new_statements.relation_note: Catalog has no record for varh1239; this is the first stress statement found for Varhadi. It documents emphatic/contrastive (focus) stress and intonation, not lexical stress placement, so it should be entered as 'emphatic stress described, word-level placement unreported', not as a claim that the language lacks word stress. Author is from Balapur, Akola district; the dialect described is the West Vidarbha (Varhad) Varhadi of Akola/Amravati/Buldhana/Washim/Yavatmal.
new_statements.rule_in_words: The thesis has a suprasegmental chapter and a stress section, but everything it says about stress is utterance-level emphasis: four kinds of 'bal' — prabal (strong) on the word that answers the question under discussion (focus stress), atiprabal (extra-strong) on the particular syllable that carries a contrast, tutak (clipped/abrupt) stress giving 'only, exactly' readings, and vilambit (prolonged) stress marking calls and intensification. No rule for where lexical word stress falls is given, and no claim that word stress is absent. The same chapter gives intonation (level, falling, rising contours, p. 69), juncture, and states that nasalized vowels and visarga of standard Marathi are absent in Varhadi. Chapter 2 adds positional vowel length: p. 35 'वरील स्वरांचे ऱ्हस्वदीर्घ उच्चार वऱ्हाडीत आढळतात मात्र, यांचे ऱ्हस्वदीर्घ स्वनिमिक नाही' (short and long realizations occur but length is not phonemic); p. 40: the nuclear vowel of a monosyllable and of the final syllable of a word is always long, the pre-final vowel of a polysyllable is short unless the word ends in a consonant / pure a. So the reading 'phrase-level prominence only' means: the only stress this source describes is phrasal/emphatic; word-level placement remains unreported.
new_statements.identity_note: Bhagwat 1967 and Kale 2010 describe the West Vidarbha (Varhad/Berar) variety around Akola (Bhagwat: 'in the neighbourhood of Akola'; Kale: author from Balapur, Akola district, dialect of Akola/Amravati/Buldhana/Washim/Yavatmal). Tryambak 2017 treats 'Varhadi' as the Marathi of the Vidarbha region generally. None covers Nagpuri specifically; the earlier-opened Jha 1972 is the Kosti caste dialect of Nagpur and neighbouring districts.

sources.note: No stress/accent statement (Contents list none; ch. I pp. 13-37 and 56-60 read as page images, pp. 38-55 are cluster lists). p. 23 gives a positional vowel-length rule: vowels long in monosyllables, short in 1st syllable and long in final syllable of disyllables, short/half-long/long in trisyllables; extra length for emphasis. Intro p. 1: Kosti is the caste dialect of the Koshti weavers of Nagpur, Bhandara, Chanda, Wardha, Yavatmal, Akola and Amravati districts.
